lossless_policy: Lossless sources only. Accepted containers: FLAC, WAV (PCM), AIFF. Rejected: MP3, Ogg Vorbis, AAC, Opus, and any transcode whose chain includes a lossy step. full_band_policy: Full-band sources only. Reject 16 kHz and other bandwidth-limited sources; upsampling does not restore missing frequencies and must never be used to make a source appear full-band. Prefer native 44.1/48 kHz recordings with documented provenance. Native rate alone is not evidence of quality: a 48 kHz FLAC may still originate from a lossy or bandwidth-limited source, so lossless provenance is assessed separately.
lossless_provenance_policy: For every candidate distinguish container format from demonstrated lossless provenance: original recording rate/bit depth where known, evidence against a lossy transcode in the chain, known processing, and unresolved questions. Insufficiently documented candidates stay needs-review or are rejected; never assume pristine.
b1_boundary_policy: B1 eligibility rules are frozen. Never resample a candidate to pass the gate. Sample-rate compatibility is recorded separately from source quality: native 44.1 kHz material stays exploratory unless the gate is formally extended. Technical eligibility is not acquisition approval and not audio quality.
gate_policy: Two gates separate authorization from acceptance. Gate A (pre-download authorization): confirm the exact source file, verify licence, permitted acquisition, and intended use from primary evidence, and resolve all rights, consent, content, and redistribution blockers BEFORE obtaining bytes; record remaining uncertainties, and do not authorize blocked candidates to enable investigation. Gate B (post-download technical acceptance): only after Gate A passes, acquire the authorized file and verify bytes, checksum, format, sample rate, bit depth, channels, duration, and source identity; inspect bandwidth and content suitability including audition; verify conversion history and category fit; reject or return to review on contradiction. No candidate has passed either gate; Gate B is not-applicable until Gate A passes.
